hero.subtitle: Defining the syntax of email messages - headers, body, addresses, and dates - the format behind every email you've ever sent or received.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
RFC 5322 defines the format of Internet email messages, specifying the syntax for headers and body. While SMTP (RFC 5321) handles delivery, this RFC defines what the message itself looks like.

An email message is just structured text: a set of header fields followed by a blank line and then the message body. MIME extensions add support for attachments and rich content.

sections.title: Header Fields
sections.content:
Header fields follow the format Field-Name: Field-Value, with long values folded across multiple lines.

FromThe author(s) of the message
ToPrimary recipient(s)
CcCarbon copy recipients
BccBlind carbon copy (not visible to other recipients)
DateDate and time the message was composed
SubjectSummary of the message topic
Message-IDGlobally unique identifier for the message
In-Reply-ToMessage-ID of the message being replied to
ReferencesThread of Message-IDs for conversation tracking

sections.title: Address Specification
sections.content:
Email addresses can be specified in several formats:

Address Formats
Simple:      user@example.com
Display:     John Doe <john@example.com>
Group:       Team: alice@ex.com, bob@ex.com;
Quoted:      "john.doe"@example.com

The local-part (before @) is case-sensitive per the standard, though most servers treat it as case-insensitive. The domain part is always case-insensitive.

sections.title: Date and Time
sections.content:
RFC 5322 defines a specific date format used in email headers:

Date Format
date-time = [ day-of-week "," ] date time

Examples:
Wed, 04 Feb 2026 10:30:00 -0500
4 Feb 2026 15:30:00 +0000

This date format is widely used beyond email. RFC 2822 dates appear in HTTP headers, RSS feeds, and many other Internet protocols.

references.text: Resnick, P., "Internet Message Format", RFC 5322, October 2008.
Freed, N. and N. Borenstein, "Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions (MIME) Part One", RFC 2045, November 1996.
